item.title: Version 2.11.1
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.11.1 — crash fix
A patch release for one serious bug: **toggling any menu-bar item in the Control Center crashed the app.**
- **Fixed: the app crashed when you switched a menu-bar item on or off.** Flipping Battery, CPU, RAM, Network or Bluetooth in the Control Center could kill the app outright. Writing the toggle's setting posted a preferences-change notification, whose handler assigned `NSStatusItem.isVisible`; AppKit persists the item's position when you do that, which posted the same notification again — an unbounded recursion that exhausted the main thread's stack. The refresh path now guards against re-entry and only writes `isVisible` on a real change. Present since v2.10.0. - **Fixed: a below-zero battery temperature read as a wildly large positive number.** IOKit reports negative values in the Temperature key as unsigned two's complement, so −5 °C came through as 42,949,667.96 °C — which also made the temperature alert fire about an overheating battery on a freezing one. Positive readings were never affected.
The unconditional `isVisible` write also meant every visible item rewrote a preference once a second; that write is gone, so an idle menu bar now touches user defaults not at all.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._

item.title: Version 2.11.0
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.11.0 — VoiceOver labels and concurrency hardening
- **The menu-bar items are readable by VoiceOver now.** Each one announces what its glyph is showing — "CPU 34%", "Battery 82%, charging", "Network up 1.2 MB/s, down 340 KB/s" — instead of being an unlabelled button. The label is refreshed only when the value actually changes, so an idle menu bar costs nothing extra. - **Thread-safety hardening across every reader.** The readers are now compiler-enforced main-thread types, and the iPhone/Android USB enumeration runs in dedicated worker actors that own their own caches. Nothing changes on screen; it removes a class of latent data races around the device caches, which were previously kept safe only by convention. - **Correct memory figures under translation.** The RAM buckets are now sized with the kernel page size rather than the process page size. Identical on native Apple Silicon and Intel Macs — it only differed for a translated process, where every bucket read four times too small. - The bundled `cocobat.py` CLI bounds its subprocess calls with a timeout instead of hanging indefinitely on a wedged `ioreg` or libimobiledevice call.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._

item.title: Version 2.10.0
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.10.0 — Reliability fixes across CPU, Network, Bluetooth, and Android
- **CPU usage no longer freezes on long uptimes:** fixed a Mach host-port leak in the CPU reader that, after a day or two of continuous running, could make the CPU readout stop updating until the app was restarted. - **Bluetooth accessory battery recovers after an off→on toggle:** the battery level of BLE accessories (e.g. a Logitech mouse) no longer sticks at its last value after you turn Bluetooth off and back on — it reconnects and resumes live updates. - **Menu-bar network rate clears on disconnect:** the throughput shown in the menu bar now drops to 0 when the connection goes away, instead of freezing at the last value while the popover already says "No active network connection". - **Intel Macs now show CPU temperature:** the classic Intel die-temperature sensors are decoded correctly (they were silently rejected before, leaving the reading blank). - **Android battery: faster reads and refresh on reconnect:** the learned battery capacity is re-read when you replug a phone, and the capacity read now filters on-device instead of transferring the multi-MB battery-history dump. - **Bluetooth device list refreshes at the intended rate:** it was updating roughly half as often as intended while the popover was open. - **Housekeeping:** de-duplicated popover components (CPU/Memory legends, the show-more toggles) and removed dead code.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._

item.title: Version 2.9.0
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.9.0
Even less background work, plus a batch of robustness fixes.
- **iPhone/iPad:** the menu-bar battery glyph now uses a lightweight read, while the heavier diagnostics read (temperature and detailed battery) runs only while the popover is open — so fewer helper processes fire when a phone is connected but you're not looking at it. Hot-battery alerts stay as responsive as before. - **Battery:** macOS's "Maximum Capacity" health figure is fetched only while the battery popover is open (it's a detail-only number), so the periodic `system_profiler` call no longer runs in the background. - **Updates:** information-only Sparkle updates now open their info page instead of offering a broken download, and a mid-download content-length change no longer skews the progress bar. - **Under the hood:** background-read timing is now on a monotonic clock (immune to system clock changes), the network-interface MAC read avoids undefined pointer access, the DNS server list renders stably when addresses repeat, and the public-IP lookup tidies up its per-fetch network session.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._

item.title: Version 2.8.0
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.8.0
Less work when you're not looking.
- **Menu-bar toggles now cut real work:** turning a metric off (Battery / CPU / RAM / Network) actually stops its background reader instead of just hiding the icon — so hiding what you don't use lowers CPU and energy. It resumes the instant you turn it back on or open the popover. - **Lower idle usage:** each menu-bar icon is redrawn only when its value changes (and never while hidden); the battery reads back off to a lazy poll — refreshed immediately on plug/unplug via a power-source notification — and the network reader stops entirely when its rate isn't on screen. - **iPhone/iPad:** far fewer background helper processes when a phone is connected but nothing is showing it, and the device's name/model are cached instead of re-read every second. - **Under the hood:** the battery and CPU sensor readers now share a single SMC connection.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._

item.title: Version 2.7.0
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.7.0
More performance and reach.
- **Network:** latency and reachability now work on IPv6-only connections. Previously the ping was IPv4-only, so an IPv6-only link showed the internet as unreachable with no latency even when it was fine. - **Lower idle usage:** iPhone/iPad and Android battery polling now backs off to a slow keep-warm when neither the popover nor the phone menu-bar item is showing — no more shelling out to libimobiledevice/adb every second for a phone nothing is watching. (Hot-battery alerts for a connected iPhone stay as responsive as before.) - **Under the hood:** the readers' background-read throttling is unified into one helper, and the SMC sensor reads skip a redundant syscall per key.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._

item.title: Version 2.6.0
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.6.0
Performance and polish.
- **Android (multi-device):** fixed battery health being dropped or misreported when more than one Android phone is connected — each device's state is now tracked independently. - **CPU:** the frequency readout no longer shows a wrong value for one tick right after reopening the popover. - **Lower idle usage:** battery power-rail/fan SMC reads and iPhone/iPad USB polling now back off while their panel is closed, cutting background work. - **UI:** the Android "show more" expand no longer stutters; removed a duplicate "Status" row in the Network panel.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._
